462.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). A Vaar with saloks; the saloks too were written by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji); (to be sung) to the tune of Tunda Asraja. Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). To my Guru I am a sacrifice, each day a hundred times over, who made gods out of men, and took no time in doing it. ॥1॥

A vaar is a hymn of pauris (stanzas); the pauris of this vaar are the First Guru's, and each is preceded by saloks, a few of them the Second Guru's (marked Mahla 2). Tunda Asraja: by tradition a prince whose hand was cut off (tunda, maimed) and who later became a king; the bards sang a vaar of him, and this vaar is set to its tune (dhuni).
463.1: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). Were a hundred moons to rise and a thousand suns to come up, even with so much light, without the Guru there is pitch darkness. ॥2॥
463.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O Nanak, those who do not keep the Guru in mind, and are clever in their own eyes, are like barren sesame plants left forsaken in an empty field. Left in the field, says Nanak, such plants have a hundred masters; the poor things flower and bear pods, yet inside their bodies is only ash. ॥3॥
Naah here is the plural of naahu (master), not the negative: barren plants left in a harvested field have no one owner, so anyone who passes may cut them and carry them off.
463.3: (God) himself made himself, and himself fashioned his Name (his glory). Second, he made the creation, and taking his seat (within it), watched its play. You are the Giver, you yourself the Maker; when pleased you give and bestow grace. You know all; having given life and its garment (the body), you will take (them) back. Taking your seat (within the creation), you have watched its play. ॥1॥
463.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). True are your lands (khand), true the universes. True are your worlds, true the forms (in them). True are your works, and all your thought. True is your rule, true your court. True is your Hukam, true your decree. True is your grace, true its token. True are the hundreds of thousands, the millions, who call on you. All rest on the True One's strength, all on the True One's might. True is your praise, true your acclaim. True is your creation, O True King. O Nanak, those who meditate on the True One are true; those who die and are born (again) are raw, raw through and through. ॥1॥
True (sacha) here means what truly is and abides: by the Darpan the salok says that God's creation is real, not an illusion, and its order lasting, though its single forms pass away.
463.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). His greatness is great, for his Name is great. His greatness is great, for his justice is true. His greatness is great, for his seat is unshakeable. His greatness is great: he knows what (all) say. His greatness is great: he grasps the feelings (of every heart). His greatness is great, for he consults no one before he gives. His greatness is great, for he is all by himself. O Nanak, (his) work cannot be told; all that he has made, the whole creation, is within his will. ॥2॥
463.6: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). This world is the chamber of the True One; the True One dwells in it. Some, by his Hukam, he takes into himself; some, by that same Hukam, he brings to ruin. Some, as it pleases him, he draws out (of Maya); others he keeps dwelling in Maya. Nor can it be told whom he will bring through. O Nanak, (this) is understood through the Guru by the one in whom he himself makes light. ॥3॥
463.7: O Nanak, having created the beings, (God) has seated Dharam Raj to write (their) accounts. There (each case) is settled by truth, truth alone; those foul with sin (jajmale) are picked out and set apart. The false find no place (there); with blackened faces they are sent off to hell. Those dyed in your Name go (from here) having won; the cheats go having lost. (God) has seated Dharam Raj to write (their) accounts. ॥2॥
Jajmale (from jazam, leprosy): the leprous; here, those foul with evil deeds.
463.8: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Wondrous are the sounds (naad), wondrous the Vedas. Wondrous are the beings, wondrous their kinds. Wondrous are the forms, wondrous the colours. Wondrous are the creatures that roam naked. Wondrous is the wind, wondrous the water. Wondrous are the fires that play their strange games. Wondrous is the earth, wondrous the sources of life (khaani). Wondrous it is that mortals cling to tastes. Wondrous is union, wondrous parting. Wondrous is hunger, wondrous the eating. Wondrous is (his) praise, wondrous (his) acclaim. Wondrous is the trackless waste, wondrous the road. Wondrous it is (that he is) near, wondrous (that he is) far. Wondrous it is (that he), ever present, watches over (all). Seeing (his) marvels, (the mind) is lost in wonder (vismaad). O Nanak, to understand (it) comes by perfect fortune. ॥1॥
Vismaad: the wonder and awe that rise in the mind at the marvels of God's creation.
464.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (Your) Kudrat is what is seen, (your) Kudrat what is heard; (your) Kudrat is fear, the essence of peace. (Your) Kudrat is in the netherworlds and the skies; (your) Kudrat is all that has form. (Your) Kudrat are the Vedas, the Puranas and the Kateb; (your) Kudrat is all thought. (Your) Kudrat is eating, drinking and clothing; (your) Kudrat is all love. (Your) Kudrat is in castes, kinds and colours; (your) Kudrat is in the beings of the world. (Your) Kudrat are the good deeds, (your) Kudrat the evil; (your) Kudrat is honour and pride. (Your) Kudrat are wind, water and fire; (your) Kudrat the earth and the dust. All is your Kudrat; you are its Master (Kadir), the Creator; pure is your glory, (and you yourself are) pure. O Nanak, (God) watches over (all) within his Hukam, and he alone, himself, pervades (all). ॥2॥

Kudrat (Arabic qudrat): power, and the creation in which God's power is at work; Kadir (Qadir) is its Master. The Kateb: the scriptures of the Semitic faiths (the Torah, the Psalms, the Gospel and the Quran).
464.2: (Man) himself enjoyed his pleasures; (then the body) became a heap of ashes, and the bhaur (the soul) departed. The worldly man died (vadda hoa); a chain was put round his neck, and he was driven off. Hereafter his deeds and his repute are read out; seated, he is made to understand the reckoning of his account. As the blows fall he finds no place (of shelter); what wailing of his is heard now? His blind mind has wasted (this human) birth. ॥3॥
The bhaur (the black bee) is a name of the soul in Gurbani. Vadda hona (to become great) is an old Punjabi idiom for dying (the Darpan).
464.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). In (God's) fear the wind blows for ever. In (God's) fear hundreds of thousands of rivers run. In (God's) fear fire does its forced labour (begaar). In (God's) fear the earth is pressed down under (its) load. In (God's) fear Indra (the god of rain) goes about on his head. In (God's) fear is the door of Dharam Raj. In (God's) fear is the sun, in (God's) fear the moon; travelling crores of kos, (their journey) has no end. In (God's) fear are the Siddhas, the Buddhas, the gods and the Naths. In (God's) fear the skies are stretched out. In (God's) fear are warriors, the mighty and the brave. In (God's) fear boatloads (of beings) come and go. Upon the heads of all, fear is written as their lot. O Nanak, only the One, the True, the Formless, is without fear. ॥1॥
Bhau (fear) in Gurbani is awe of God and of his Hukam, under which all creation keeps its course. Begaar: labour forced from one without pay. A kos is an old measure of distance, about two miles.
464.4: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O Nanak, the Formless One (alone) is without fear; so many other Rams are (but) dust (before him). So many are the tales of Kaanh, so many the reflections on the Vedas. So many beggars dance, and wheeling round and round keep the beat. The players (bajaari) come into the bazaar and set out their show. They sing (as) kings and queens, and talk wild nonsense. (They wear) earrings worth a lakh of takas, necklaces worth a lakh of takas; (but) the bodies they are put on, O Nanak, those bodies turn to ash. Wisdom is not found by talk; to tell of it is as hard as iron. It is gained only when it comes by (his) grace; all other cleverness and command come to nothing. ॥2॥

Bajaari (by the Darpan, the raasdharis): troupes who staged the raas in the bazaars for a living, acting out in song and dance the stories of Krishna and the gopis, and of Ram and Sita; the two saloks at 465.2 and 465.3 also speak of the raas. A taka was a coin.
465.1: If you cast your glance of grace, then by (your) grace the True Guru is found. This soul roamed through many births; then the True Guru made it hear the Shabad. None is a giver as great as the True Guru; listen, all you people, every one. Those who rid themselves of self within have found the True One by meeting the True Guru, (the Guru) who has made (them) understand the True One, Truth itself. ॥4॥
465.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The gharis are all gopis, the pahars (of day and night) Kaanh, Gopal; wind, water and fire are the ornaments, the moon and the sun the avatars; the whole earth is (the play's) goods and wealth, and all the world's entanglements are the things it uses. O Nanak, (the world,) empty of wisdom, is being robbed; Jamkaal has devoured it. ॥1॥
465.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The disciples play (the instruments), and the gurus dance; they jig their feet and toss their heads; the dust flies up and settles in their hair. The onlookers watch, laugh, and make for home. For the sake of bread they keep the beat, and fling themselves upon the ground. They sing as the gopis, they sing as Kaanh, they sing as Sita and as Ram the king. The Fearless, the Formless, whose Name is True, whose making is all the world: him those servants serve whom (his) grace has uplifted; for those whose minds are eager (for him), the night (of life) is dew-soaked and sweet. Those who have learned this teaching through reflection on the Guru's word, the Gracious One, in his kindness, carries (them) across. The oil-press, the spinning wheel, the grindstone, the potter's wheel, the whirlwinds of the desert, many beyond count, tops, churning-staves, threshing frames, birds that wheel without pausing for breath, creatures set on a spike and spun round: O Nanak, of those that go round there is no count and no end. Binding (beings) in bonds, he spins them round; everyone dances by the deeds that have fallen to his lot. Those who laugh as they dance depart in tears. (Dancing,) they neither take flight (to a higher state) nor become Siddhas. Dancing and leaping are (but) the mind's fancy; O Nanak, those whose minds hold (God's) fear hold (his) love in their minds. ॥2॥
465.4: Your Name is Nirankar (the Formless); taking (your) Name, one does not go to hell. Soul and body, all is his; give (of what he gives) and then eat; speak of (the giving), and (its merit) is lost. If you want your own good, do good deeds and (still) be called lowly. Even if a mighty man would cast it off, old age comes on, putting on its garb. No one stays (here) when the measure (paai) of life is full. ॥5॥
465.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). With the Muslims it is the praise of the Shariat (the Islamic law); reading it again and again, they reflect: (God's) servants are those who enter its bond (bandi) to behold (his) vision. The Hindus praise the Praiseworthy One, through the darshans (their schools of scripture), as beautiful and boundless; they bathe at the tiraths, make offerings (to images) and worship (them), with the scent of aloe-wood and perfumes. The yogis, all of them, meditate on the Creator in Sunn, naming him Alakh (the Unseen); (yet in their meditation) the One of subtle form, whose Name is Niranjan, takes the shape of a body. In the minds of the charitable, contentment springs up at the thought of giving; (but) giving and giving, they ask a thousandfold (in return), and the world sings their praise. Thieves, adulterers and liars, the wicked and the sinful: some use up what they had and go from here; they too have some task (given them). In water and on land are beings, in the realms and the worlds, form upon form: what they say, you alone know; they too are in your care. O Nanak, the devotees hunger to praise (you); the True Name is (their) support. Ever in bliss they live, day and night, (as) dust beneath the feet of the virtuous. ॥1॥
The salok first tells the ways of the Muslims, the Hindus, the yogis, the givers and the wicked; the Guru's own conclusion is in its last two lines (the Darpan, the Santhya).
466.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The clay of a Muslim('s grave) may come to lie in the potter's lump; shaping it, (he) makes pots and bricks of it, and as it burns (in the kiln) it cries out. The poor thing weeps as it burns and burns, and embers keep dropping from it. O Nanak, the Creator who made the creation, he alone knows (its secret). ॥2॥
The salok answers a belief held among Muslims, that those whose bodies are burnt burn in the fire of hell (the Darpan).
466.2: Without the True Guru no one has found (God); without the True Guru no one has found (him). (God) has placed himself within the True Guru, and has made this plain and proclaimed it. One who has rid himself of attachment within is free for ever, when the True Guru is met. Best of all is this understanding: one who has fixed his mind on the True One has found the Giver, the Life of the world. ॥6॥
466.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). In Haumai (ego) one comes (into the world), in Haumai one goes. In Haumai one is born, in Haumai one dies. In Haumai one gives, in Haumai one takes. In Haumai one earns, in Haumai one loses. In Haumai one is (now) truthful, (now) false. In Haumai one weighs sin and merit. In Haumai one falls (now) into hell, (now) into heaven. In Haumai one laughs, in Haumai one weeps. In Haumai one is soiled (with sin), in Haumai one washes (it off). In Haumai, (proud of) caste and kind, one loses (oneself). In Haumai one is (now) a fool, in Haumai (now) wise, (but) does not grasp what liberation and release are. In Haumai one (chases) Maya, in Haumai (lives under) its shadow. Acting in Haumai again and again, beings are born (again and again). When one understands Haumai, then the (Lord's) door comes into sight. Without this knowledge, one only quarrels, talking and talking. O Nanak, this record is written by the Hukam: as (beings) look (upon others), so their own form becomes. ॥1॥
Hau (I) and Haumai (I-am-ness): the sense of a self apart from God.
466.4: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). Such is the nature of Haumai: (beings) do the deeds of Haumai. These are the bonds of Haumai: (beings) fall into the life-forms again and again. Where does Haumai spring from? By what discipline does it go? Haumai is by this very Hukam: driven by their past deeds, (beings) wander. Haumai is a long, lingering disease, but it has a cure as well. If (God) shows his grace, then (beings) live by the Guru's Shabad. Nanak says: hear, O people; by this discipline the pains (of Haumai) go. ॥2॥
466.5: Service has been done by the contented, who have meditated on none but the True One. They have not set foot on (the path of) evil; doing good deeds, they have lived by dharma. They have broken the world's bonds, and have taken little of grain and water. (O Lord,) you are the great Giver of gifts; you give each day, and (your giving) ever grows. By praising (you), they have found (you), the Great One. ॥7॥
467.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Of men, trees, tiraths, riverbanks, clouds and fields, of islands, worlds, spheres, continents and universes, of the sources of life, egg-born, womb-born, earth-born and sweat-born, of lakes, mountains and creatures, he knows the measure, O Nanak. O Nanak, having brought forth the beings, (God) takes care of them all. The Creator who made the creation must also see to its care. That Creator who brought forth the world takes thought for it. To him I bow, hail to him; his court stands for ever unbroken. O Nanak, without the True Name, what is the frontal mark, what the sacred thread? ॥1॥
467.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Lakhs of good deeds and kindnesses, lakhs of acts of merit approved (by the world), lakhs of austerities at tiraths, yoga in the stillness of Sahaj in the wilds, lakhs of feats of valour, the breath of life let go on the field of battle, lakhs of ways of fixing the attention, lakhs of (discourses on) knowledge and of meditations, and the Puranas read and recited: (before) the Creator who made the creation and wrote down (all) coming and going, O Nanak, (all these) clevernesses are worthless; his grace is the true mark (of acceptance). ॥2॥
467.3: (O Lord,) you alone are the True Master, who have made Truth, nothing but Truth, prevail. Whoever you give it to receives Truth; then such ones live the Truth. Those in whose hearts (the Guru) has set Truth to dwell have found Truth through meeting the True Guru. Fools do not know the Truth; the manmukhs have wasted their lives. Why did (such a one) come into the world? ॥8॥
467.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). One may read and read till carts are loaded, read and read till caravans are filled (with books); read and read till a boat is laden, read and read till pits are packed full; one may read for as many years as there are, year upon year, read for as many months as there are; one may read for as long as life lasts, read for as many breaths as there are: (Even so,) O Nanak, in (God's) reckoning one thing alone counts; all else is the idle babble of Haumai. ॥1॥
467.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). However much one writes and reads, so much does one fret and burn (within). However many tiraths one tours, so much the more one prattles. (One) has put on many guises and given the body pain: endure, O soul, what you have done yourself. (One who) has eaten no grain has lost the taste (of life); he has suffered much pain, for something other (than the Name) has pleased him. (One) wears no clothes, and is in torment day and night. (One) has gone astray in silence: asleep, how can he wake without the Guru? (One) goes barefoot, and reaps what he has done. (One) has eaten what is foul and put ash on his head: the blind fool has lost his honour. Without the Name, nothing is accepted. (One) lives in the wilds, at tombs and cremation grounds: the blind man does not know (the way), and afterwards repents. One who meets the True Guru finds peace, and enshrines the Lord's Name in the mind. O Nanak, one on whom (God) casts his glance of grace finds (the Guru); free from hope and anxiety, he burns away Haumai through the Shabad. ॥2॥
468.1: (O Lord,) your devotees are dear to your mind; singing (your) praises, they look beautiful at (your) door. O Nanak, those without (his) grace find no shelter at the door; they wander about. Some do not understand their own origin, and, having nothing, make much of themselves. I am a humble minstrel (dhadhi) of low caste; others call themselves high-born. (The company of) those who meditate on you is what I ask for. ॥9॥
468.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The king is falsehood, the subjects are falsehood, all the world is falsehood. Pavilions are falsehood, palaces are falsehood, and he who sits in them is falsehood. Gold is falsehood, silver is falsehood, and he who wears them is falsehood. The body is falsehood, clothes are falsehood, and beauty beyond measure is falsehood. Husband is falsehood, wife is falsehood; worn out (in it), they come to ruin. The false one's love is fixed in falsehood, and he has forgotten the Creator. With whom should one make friends? The whole world is passing away. Falsehood is sweet, falsehood is honey; falsehood drowns the whole boatload (of beings). Nanak humbly prays: without you, (all) is falsehood, nothing but falsehood. ॥1॥
Kur in this salok is a noun: not a lie told, but what is unreal and passes away, the world's show of illusion; kurai: of the false one, the being caught in it.
468.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Truth is known only when the True One is in the heart; (then) the filth of falsehood comes off, and (one) washes the body clean. Truth is known only when (one) bears love for the True One; hearing the Name, the mind blossoms with joy, and then one finds the door of liberation. Truth is known only when the soul knows the (true) way of life: making ready the earth of the body, it puts into it the Creator's seed (the Name). Truth is known only when (one) takes true teaching (from the Guru), knows how to show compassion to living beings, and gives something in charity and good works. Truth is known only when (one) dwells at the tirath of the soul within, and, having asked the True Guru, stays seated (there) and makes his home (there). Truth is the cure for all (ills); it washes sins away and drives them out. Nanak humbly prays before those who have Truth in their lap. ॥2॥
468.4: For me the gift (to ask for) is the dust from beneath (the Sants') feet; if it is obtained, let it be put to the forehead. Let false greed be given up, and, single-minded, let the Unseen One be meditated on. Such fruit is reaped as is the work one does. If it is so written from the start, then the dust of such ones is obtained. (Leaning on one's) small understanding, service is lost. ॥10॥
468.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). A famine of Truth has come, falsehood holds sway; in the blackness of Kalyug, (people have become) ghouls. Those who sowed the seed (of the Name) have gone with honour; how now can split grain sprout? Seed sprouts if it is whole, and the season too is the best of seasons. O Nanak, without the mordant, raw cloth does not take the (fast) colour. In the fear (of God) let (the mind) be set on the khumb, and let effort be the mordant for the cloth (of the body). O Nanak, if (the mind) is dyed in devotion, not a trace of falsehood (remains). ॥1॥
Khumb: the dyer's vat in which cloth is steamed clean before dyeing. Saram here is effort, as in the Saram Khand of the Japji.
468.6: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Greed and sin are the two, king and minister (mahta), and falsehood has become the chief (sikdar). Lust is the deputy (naib), summoned and consulted; he sits with them, deliberating again and again. The subjects, blind and without knowledge, stuff the fire (of the rulers' craving) with carrion (bribes). Those (called) wise dance, play instruments, put on guises and adorn themselves. They shout aloud, sing of battles, and expound the tales of warriors. Foolish pandits love to amass (wealth) by cunning and argument. The pious do pious deeds and waste them, asking (in return) for the door of liberation. (Some) call themselves celibates but do not know the way; they leave hearth and home and sit (apart). Everyone is perfect in his own eyes; no one calls himself lacking. O Nanak, only when the weight of honour (from God) is put in the other pan does (one) prove truly weighed. ॥2॥
469.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). What is ordained, O Nanak, shall sound forth (come to light); the True One himself watches over (all). All have made their leaps (and tried their strength), but what the Creator does, that comes to pass. Hereafter there is no caste and no force; hereafter the beings (one meets) are new (strangers). Those few whose honour counts in the reckoning, they alone are good. ॥3॥
469.2: Those on whom you cast your grace from the very first have then meditated on the Master. It is not in these creatures' power to do anything; you have brought forth a world of many kinds. Some you unite (with yourself); others you have led astray from yourself. By the Guru's grace you are known (by the one) to whom you have made yourself understood, and (that one) has merged, in Sahaj, in the True One. ॥11॥
469.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Sorrow has become the remedy and comfort the disease, for when there is comfort, then (your remembrance) is not there. You are the Creator, the Doer (of all); I am nothing; when I would do (anything) myself, it does not come about. ॥1॥
469.4: I am a sacrifice to you, who dwell within your creation; your limit cannot be perceived.
This salok has a Rahao line of its own between its two parts, as a shabad has; it holds the salok's central thought.
469.5: Your light is in the creation, and in every light you are known; undivided and whole, you fill all things. You are the True Master, and lovely is your praise; whoever has offered it has crossed over. Says Nanak, (all these are) the Creator's doings: whatever is to be done, he is doing. ॥2॥
469.6: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). The way of the yogi is knowledge; the way of the Brahmins is the Veda; the way of the Khatri is valour; the way of the Shudra is the service of others; the way of all is (the remembrance of) the One; if anyone knows this secret, Nanak is his servant; he himself is (the image of) Niranjan, the Lord. ॥3॥
Sabadam here is the way, the duty (dharma), laid down for each.
469.7: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). The one Krishna (the Lord) is the soul of all the gods, and the soul too of the gods of the gods; (in all) is the soul of Vasudev (the Lord); if anyone knows this secret, Nanak is his servant; he himself is (the image of) Niranjan, the Lord. ॥4॥
Krishna here is a name of the one God.
469.8: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Water stays held only within a pitcher, (yet) without water no pitcher is made; (so) the mind stays steady only when held by wisdom, (yet) without the Guru there is no wisdom. ॥5॥
469.9: If the learned one is a sinner, the unlettered one who is good is not punished. As are the deeds one labours at, so is the name one comes to be known by. Let no such game be played as would make one lose on reaching the Lord's court. Of the learned and the unlettered alike, the case is weighed hereafter; whoever goes headstrong, by his own will, is punished hereafter. ॥12॥
Omi (Arabic ummi): unlettered, one who cannot read or write.
470.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O Nanak, the body that is the meru (the crown of all bodies, the human one) has one chariot and one charioteer; age after age they are changed again; the wise understand this. In Satjug the chariot is of contentment, and dharma the charioteer in front; in Treta the chariot is of continence, and might the charioteer in front; in Duapar the chariot is of austerity, and sat (upright conduct) the charioteer in front; in Kalyug the chariot is of fire, and falsehood the charioteer in front. ॥1॥

Meru: the mountain at the centre of the earth in the Puranas, and the head bead of a rosary; hence the chief, the best. The body as a chariot with a charioteer is the image of the Katha Upanishad; here the chariot is the bent of people's nature in each age, and the charioteer what leads it.
470.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The Sama (Veda) calls the Master Setambar (the white-robed), who dwells in truth; (in its age, people) abide in truth; everyone merges in the Truth. The Rig (Veda) says: (Ram) pervades all; among the gods, the Name of Ram is the sun; by taking the Name, sins depart; O Nanak, then (people) attain liberation. In the Yajur (Veda), Chandravali was beguiled by force, and (the Master's name) became Kaanh Krishna, the Yadav; he brought the Parjat (tree) for the gopi, and made merry in Brindaban. In Kalyug the Atharva Veda came (to the fore), and (the Master's) name became Khuda and Allah; taking blue cloth, they wore garments (of it), and the Turks and Pathans held sway. All four Vedas came to be (held) true; those who read and ponder them find four (different) teachings (in them). One who, worshipping with loving devotion, calls himself lowly, then, O Nanak, attains liberation. ॥2॥

The four Vedas are set beside the four ages: the Sama with Satjug, the Rig with Treta, the Yajur with Duapar, the Atharva with Kalyug, each with the name of the Lord that then prevailed: Setambar, Ram, Krishna, Allah. Chandravali: by tradition a gopi of Braj whom Krishna loved. The Parjat: the wish-fulfilling tree of Indra's heaven, which by the Puranas Krishna brought down to earth for his queen Satyabhama. Blue was the dress of the Turk and Pathan rulers of the time.
470.3: I am a sacrifice to the True Guru, meeting whom (I have) kept the Master in mind; who, giving his teaching, has given (me) the collyrium of wisdom, by which with these eyes (I) have seen the world (as it is). Those traders who left the Master and clung to another have drowned. The True Guru is the ship; rare is the one who has understood (this); (him the Guru) in his grace has carried across. ॥13॥
470.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The simmal tree is straight, very tall and very stout; (the birds) that come to it in hope: why do they go away disappointed? (Because) its fruits are insipid, its flowers tasteless, and its leaves of no use. O Nanak, sweetness and lowliness are the very core of virtues and good deeds. Everyone bows for his own sake; no one bows for another's. Put on the scales and weighed, the (pan) that sinks is the heavier. The sinner who slays deer bows double; (but) what comes of bowing the head, when (people) go on with impure hearts? ॥1॥
The simmal (silk-cotton) tree: tall, straight and bright with red flowers, but its fruit holds nothing to eat, only floss.
470.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (The pandit) reads the books, says the sandhya prayers, and disputes; he worships stone (idols), and sits in trance like a heron; lies are on his lips, (decked out) like fine ornaments; three times a day he ponders the three-footed (Gayatri); a rosary round his neck, a tilak on his brow; two dhotis, and a cloth over his head. If he knew the work of (worshipping) God, (he would see that) all these rites are surely hollow. Says Nanak, one should meditate (on God) with firm faith, (but) without the True Guru one does not find the way. ॥2॥

Sandhya: the Brahmin's prayers and rites at dawn, noon and dusk; the three-footed one (traipal) is the Gayatri, the Rig Veda verse in three parts recited at them. The heron stands still in the water as if in trance, but is watching for fish.
470.6: Leaving the lovely garment (of the body) and its beauty in the world, one has to go; the bad and the good one has done, one must oneself reap. (One who) gave orders as his mind pleased must go hereafter by a narrow road; stripped bare, he is driven to hell, and then he looks dreadful indeed. Having done wrong, he must repent. ॥14॥
471.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Compassion the cotton, contentment the thread, continence the knots and upright conduct the twist: such is the soul's sacred thread; O pandit, if you have it, put it on (me). It does not break, no dirt clings to it, it is not burned, nor is it lost. Blessed, O Nanak, are the people who go (on their way) wearing it round their necks. (This thread) you had brought for four cowries and, seated in the chauka, put it on (your patron); you whispered instruction in (his) ear, and the Brahmin became (his) guru. He died, it fell away, and he went without a thread. ॥1॥
Chaukar: four cowries; the cowrie shell was the smallest money.
471.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (One commits) countless thefts, countless adulteries, countless lies and countless abuses; countless frauds and breaches of trust, kept secret within, night and day. From cotton the thread is spun; the Brahmin comes and twists it; a goat is killed, cooked and eaten, and everyone says: (the thread) is on. When it grows old it is cast aside, and then another is put on. O Nanak, were there strength in the thread, the thread would not break. ॥2॥
471.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). By believing in the Name, honour springs up; praise (of God) is the true thread; (with it, honour) is gained in the Lord's court; this pure thread will not break. ॥3॥
471.4: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). There is no thread on the senses, no thread (to hold him back) from women; (so) morning after morning his beard is spat upon. No thread on the feet, no thread on the hands; no thread on the tongue, no thread on the eyes. Without a thread himself he wanders about, yet twisting threads, he puts them on others. He takes a fee and performs marriages, and, taking out his almanac, shows (people) the way. Hear and see, O people, this wonder: blind in mind, and his name is Wise. ॥4॥
471.5: When the Master grows merciful and shows grace, he will have (one) do that very work (which pleases him). That servant alone serves whom (the Master) makes obey his Hukam. By obeying the Hukam (he) is approved, and then he will reach the Master's mansion. Doing what pleases the Master, he will gain the fruit his mind longed for; then he will go to the Lord's court robed in honour. ॥15॥
471.6: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). You levy a tax on the cow and the Brahmin; by the cow-dung (you plaster with) no one crosses over. Dhoti, tilak and rosary (you wear), (yet) you eat the grain of the mlechhas. Indoors you worship, (outside) you read the Kateb; your way of life, brother, is the Turks'. Give up these hypocrisies; taking the Naam, you will cross over. ॥1॥

By the commentaries, these lines speak to the Hindu officials of the Muslim rulers, who levied the rulers' tax even on cows and Brahmins and yet kept the rites of purity: the kitchen square plastered with cow-dung, the dhoti, tilak and rosary. Mlechh: impure, alien; the caste Hindus' word for foreigners, here the Muslim rulers.
471.7: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Those who devour men say the namaz; those who ply the knife have the sacred thread at their necks. In their homes the Brahmins blow the conch; they too relish the same flavours. False is the capital, false the trade; by speaking lies they get their food. Modesty and dharma dwell far away (from them); O Nanak, falsehood fills every place. A tilak on the forehead, an ochre dhoti round the waist, (and) a knife in the hand: (they are) butchers of the world. Wearing blue clothes, they find favour (with the rulers); taking their bread from the mlechhas, they worship the Puranas. Their food is a goat slaughtered with the words of a foreign tongue, (yet they say:) no one is to step onto our chauka. The chauka is laid out and a line drawn (around it); and the false ones come and sit upon it. (They say:) take care, lest it be defiled, lest it be defiled; this food of ours will be spoiled. With defiled bodies they do wicked deeds, and with soiled minds they rinse their mouths. Says Nanak, let the True One be meditated on; if there is purity, then the True One is found. ॥2॥

The devourers of men: by the commentaries, the officials of the time who preyed on the people by bribes and oppression; those with the knife and the sacred thread are their Hindu clerks. The foreign tongue (abhakhia): Arabic, in which the kalma is recited as the goat is slaughtered halal. Chuli: a handful of water sipped and rinsed in the mouth for ritual purity.
472.1: (God) holds everyone in his mind, and, watching (them), moves them along under his eye. He himself bestows greatness, and he himself has (beings) do their deeds. Greater than the great is he, and vast his earth; one by one he sets each to his task. If he turns his look against them, he makes sultans (worth no more than) grass; they beg at the door, and no one puts alms (in their bowl). ॥16॥
472.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If a thief robs a house, and, having robbed it, gives (the goods) for his forebears, then in the world beyond the goods are recognised, and (so) he makes thieves of his forebears. The hands of the go-between (the Brahmin) are cut off: such is the justice (God) does. O Nanak, in the world beyond one receives only what one earns, toils for and gives (with one's own hands). ॥1॥

Pitars: dead forebears. In the shraadh rite, food and goods are given to a Brahmin for them, in the belief that they reach the forebears; the Brahmin who takes them is the go-between (dalal) of this salok.
472.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). As a woman's monthly course comes to her time after time, (so) in the mouth of the false dwells the defilement (of falsehood), and day after day he comes to grief. They are not called pure who (merely) wash the body and sit down (as pure); O Nanak, they alone are pure in whose mind he (God) has come to dwell. ॥2॥
472.4: (Those who have) saddled horses swift as the wind, and harems decked out in every colour, (who) have set up houses, pavilions and mansions and sit (in them), having spread out a display, (who) take the pleasures their minds desire, but do not know the Lord: they lose (the game of life). Giving orders, they ate (their fill), and gazing at their palaces forgot death; old age came upon them, undone by their youth. ॥17॥
472.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If Sutak is to be believed in, then Sutak is everywhere: in cow-dung and in wood, too, the worm comes to life; of all the grains of corn there are, not one is without life; first of all, water itself is a living thing, by which every being is kept green (alive). How then can Sutak be kept away? Sutak falls in the very kitchen. O Nanak, Sutak is not removed in this way; (divine) knowledge washes it off. ॥1॥
In a house under sutak, its food and water are not touched and no rites are performed.
472.6: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The Sutak of the mind is greed; the Sutak of the tongue is falsehood; the Sutak of the eyes is gazing on the beauty of another's wife and on another's wealth; the Sutak of the ears is that (people) backbite and it falls into the ears. O Nanak, (such) men, (though they look as white) as swans, go bound to the city of Jam. ॥2॥
472.7: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). All Sutak is doubt (superstition); it clings to those who have gone after another (than God). Birth and death are (God's) Hukam; by his will (a being) comes and goes. Eating and drinking are pure: (God) has gathered sustenance and given it (to all). O Nanak, those who have understood (this) through the Guru are touched by no Sutak. ॥3॥
473.1: Let us praise the True Guru as great, in whom are great excellences. When the Husband Lord brought (us) together (with the Guru), then (those excellences) came into sight; when it pleased him, (he) set them to dwell in the mind. By his command, laying his hand on (our) forehead, he struck the evils out from within. With the Husband Lord pleased, the nine treasures were found. ॥18॥
473.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). First (the Brahmin) makes himself pure, and comes and sits in the pure (chauka); before him, the pure one, is set (food) that no one has gone near to defile. Pure, he eats, and begins to chant a salok; (yet the food) is thrown into a foul place (the belly): on whom does this blame fall? Grain is a god, water is a god, fire is a god, salt (is a god); the fifth, ghee, was added, and then (the food) became clean and holy. (Then this) body (of the gods) met with the sinner, and was spat upon. The mouth with which (people) do not utter the Naam, and without the Name eat dainties: O Nanak, know it in the same way: on that mouth spittle falls. ॥1॥
473.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Of woman we are born, within woman we are formed, to woman we are betrothed and wed; through woman friendships are made, through woman the way (of the world) goes on; if a woman dies, (another) woman is sought; through woman the bonds (of kinship) are tied. Why should she be called bad, of whom kings are born? Of woman, woman herself is born; without woman there is no one. O Nanak, the True One alone stands outside woman (unborn of her). The mouth with which (God) is ever praised glows with the beauty of good fortune; O Nanak, those faces are radiant in that True Court. ॥2॥
Bhand is here an old word for woman, not the jester (bhand) of present-day speech.
473.4: Everyone claims (things) as his own; the one who does not is to be sought out and singled out. For what each has done, each must himself settle the account. Since we are not to stay in this world, why wear ourselves out in pride? Call no one bad: having read the letters, this is what is to be understood; do not quarrel with a fool. ॥19॥
473.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O Nanak, by speaking harshly, body and mind grow harsh. The harsh one is known as harsh, and harsh is the harsh one's repute; the harsh one is cast out of the Lord's court, and spittle falls on the harsh one's face; the harsh one is called a fool, and is punished with (a beating of) shoes. ॥1॥
473.6: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Those who are false within, keep up an honour outside and make a show in the world: though they bathe at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage, their filth does not come off. Those with silk within and rags without are the good ones in the world; their love is set on God, and they dwell on the thought of seeing him. In (his) love they laugh, in love they weep, and they fall silent too; they care for no one but the True Master. On the road (of life) they ask at his door for provisions, and eat when he gives. There is one court and one pen, and there we and you (all) are to meet; at that door he takes the account, and, O Nanak, (the false) are crushed as seeds are crushed for oil. ॥2॥
474.1: You yourself made the creation, and you yourself have set your power (in it). Setting out the pieces, raw and ripe, you watch what you have made. Whoever has come will depart; each one (goes) when his turn has come. Why put out of mind the Master to whom our soul and breath belong? With our own hands, by ourselves, let us put our own task in order. ॥20॥
474.2: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). What kind of love is this, that goes and attaches itself to another? O Nanak, he is called a lover who stays ever absorbed (in the Beloved). One who takes it as good when good comes, and turns sour when ill comes: such a one is not called a lover; he deals by keeping accounts. ॥1॥
474.3: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). One who both bows in salute and answers back (to the Master) has gone astray from the very start. O Nanak, both are false; neither is accepted. ॥2॥
474.4: The Master by serving whom peace is found: let us keep him ever in mind. Since what we have done (comes back) to us, why labour at what is evil? Let us do no evil at all, and look far ahead. Let us cast the dice in such a way that we do not lose (the game) with the Master; let us labour at something that brings profit. ॥21॥
474.5: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). (If) a servant is at his service, and with it is proud and quarrelsome, (and) talks a great deal, he does not win the Master's pleasure. If he gives up his self and serves, then he gains some honour; O Nanak, he meets the one he serves; (so) engaged, he is accepted. ॥1॥
474.6: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). What is in the heart is what sprouts; what the mouth says is (mere) wind. One sows poison and asks for Amrit: see what justice this is. ॥2॥
474.7: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). Friendship with the ignorant never turns out well; as he understands, so he behaves; let anyone weigh it and see. One thing goes into another only when what was there is set aside. With the Master no command prevails; it is prayer, offered (to him), that befits. Practising falsehood, falsehood alone comes of it; O Nanak, through (God's) praise (the mind) blossoms. ॥3॥
474.8: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). Friendship with the ignorant, and love for one far greater (than oneself), are like a line drawn in water, which leaves neither place nor trace. ॥4॥
474.9: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). If one who is ignorant takes up a task, he cannot bring it to a good end; even if he does one thing or so well, he spoils the next all the same. ॥5॥
474.10: A servant is (truly) at service if he walks as the Master wishes; he receives great honour, and draws double wages besides. (If) he sets himself up as the Master's equal, he then falls into disgrace; he loses the wages he had, and is struck with shoes on the face. He whose gifts we eat: to him let us give praise. O Nanak, with the Master no command prevails; prayer prevails. ॥22॥
474.11: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). What kind of gift is it that one gets of oneself (by one's own effort)? O Nanak, that is grace (karamat) which comes when the Master is pleased. ॥1॥
Karamat is here a gift of grace, not a miracle: it answers the daat (gift) of the line before.
475.1: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). What kind of service is this, that does not take away the fear of the Master? O Nanak, the one to be called a servant is he who merges into the Master. ॥2॥
475.2: O Nanak, no end is seen to the Lord's near and far shores. He himself brings about the making, and then he himself brings about the destroying. Round the necks of some are chains; many ride on horses. He himself causes and he himself does; to whom am I to complain? O Nanak, he who made the creation: it is he again who must care for it. ॥23॥
475.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (God) himself fashioned the vessels (of the body), and he himself fills them. Some hold milk, while others stay up on the hearth; some lie down and sleep on quilts, while others stay standing over them (in attendance). He sets right those, O Nanak, on whom he looks with grace. ॥1॥
475.4: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). He himself fashions, he himself makes, and he himself keeps, too, what he has brought forth; creating beings within it, he watches them, setting up and pulling down. To whom can we speak, O Nanak? He himself is all in all. ॥2॥
475.5: Of the greatness of the Great One, nothing at all can be said. He is the Creator, the Master of creation, the Bountiful (Karim); he carries their sustenance to all beings. (All beings) do the work that he himself has allotted (to them) from the very start. O Nanak, apart from the One there is no other place; he does whatever is his will.
Sudh (corrected): written after the closing numbers of the vaar, it marks that the text was checked against the original.

462.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
A Vaar with saloks; the saloks too were written by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji); (to be sung) to the tune of Tunda Asraja.
Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
To my Guru I am a sacrifice, each day a hundred times over,
who made gods out of men, and took no time in doing it. ॥1॥
463.1: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
Were a hundred moons to rise and a thousand suns to come up,
even with so much light, without the Guru there is pitch darkness. ॥2॥
463.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, those who do not keep the Guru in mind, and are clever in their own eyes,
are like barren sesame plants left forsaken in an empty field.
Left in the field, says Nanak, such plants have a hundred masters;
the poor things flower and bear pods, yet inside their bodies is only ash. ॥3॥
463.3: (God) himself made himself, and himself fashioned his Name (his glory).
Second, he made the creation, and taking his seat (within it), watched its play.
You are the Giver, you yourself the Maker; when pleased you give and bestow grace.
You know all; having given life and its garment (the body), you will take (them) back.
Taking your seat (within the creation), you have watched its play. ॥1॥
463.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
True are your lands (khand), true the universes.
True are your worlds, true the forms (in them).
True are your works, and all your thought.
True is your rule, true your court.
True is your Hukam, true your decree.
True is your grace, true its token.
True are the hundreds of thousands, the millions, who call on you.
All rest on the True One's strength, all on the True One's might.
True is your praise, true your acclaim.
True is your creation, O True King.
O Nanak, those who meditate on the True One are true;
those who die and are born (again) are raw, raw through and through. ॥1॥
463.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
His greatness is great, for his Name is great.
His greatness is great, for his justice is true.
His greatness is great, for his seat is unshakeable.
His greatness is great: he knows what (all) say.
His greatness is great: he grasps the feelings (of every heart).
His greatness is great, for he consults no one before he gives.
His greatness is great, for he is all by himself.
O Nanak, (his) work cannot be told;
all that he has made, the whole creation, is within his will. ॥2॥
463.6: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
This world is the chamber of the True One; the True One dwells in it.
Some, by his Hukam, he takes into himself; some, by that same Hukam, he brings to ruin.
Some, as it pleases him, he draws out (of Maya); others he keeps dwelling in Maya.
Nor can it be told whom he will bring through.
O Nanak, (this) is understood through the Guru by the one in whom he himself makes light. ॥3॥
463.7: O Nanak, having created the beings, (God) has seated Dharam Raj to write (their) accounts.
There (each case) is settled by truth, truth alone; those foul with sin (jajmale) are picked out and set apart.
The false find no place (there); with blackened faces they are sent off to hell.
Those dyed in your Name go (from here) having won; the cheats go having lost.
(God) has seated Dharam Raj to write (their) accounts. ॥2॥
463.8: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Wondrous are the sounds (naad), wondrous the Vedas.
Wondrous are the beings, wondrous their kinds.
Wondrous are the forms, wondrous the colours.
Wondrous are the creatures that roam naked.
Wondrous is the wind, wondrous the water.
Wondrous are the fires that play their strange games.
Wondrous is the earth, wondrous the sources of life (khaani).
Wondrous it is that mortals cling to tastes.
Wondrous is hunger, wondrous the eating.
Wondrous is the trackless waste, wondrous the road.
Wondrous it is (that he is) near, wondrous (that he is) far.
Wondrous it is (that he), ever present, watches over (all).
Seeing (his) marvels, (the mind) is lost in wonder (vismaad).
O Nanak, to understand (it) comes by perfect fortune. ॥1॥
464.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(Your) Kudrat is what is seen, (your) Kudrat what is heard; (your) Kudrat is fear, the essence of peace.
(Your) Kudrat is in the netherworlds and the skies; (your) Kudrat is all that has form.
(Your) Kudrat are the Vedas, the Puranas and the Kateb; (your) Kudrat is all thought.
(Your) Kudrat is eating, drinking and clothing; (your) Kudrat is all love.
(Your) Kudrat is in castes, kinds and colours; (your) Kudrat is in the beings of the world.
(Your) Kudrat are the good deeds, (your) Kudrat the evil; (your) Kudrat is honour and pride.
(Your) Kudrat are wind, water and fire; (your) Kudrat the earth and the dust.
All is your Kudrat; you are its Master (Kadir), the Creator; pure is your glory, (and you yourself are) pure.
O Nanak, (God) watches over (all) within his Hukam, and he alone, himself, pervades (all). ॥2॥
464.2: (Man) himself enjoyed his pleasures; (then the body) became a heap of ashes, and the bhaur (the soul) departed.
The worldly man died (vadda hoa); a chain was put round his neck, and he was driven off.
Hereafter his deeds and his repute are read out; seated, he is made to understand the reckoning of his account.
As the blows fall he finds no place (of shelter); what wailing of his is heard now?
His blind mind has wasted (this human) birth. ॥3॥
464.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
In (God's) fear the wind blows for ever.
In (God's) fear hundreds of thousands of rivers run.
In (God's) fear fire does its forced labour (begaar).
In (God's) fear the earth is pressed down under (its) load.
In (God's) fear Indra (the god of rain) goes about on his head.
In (God's) fear is the door of Dharam Raj.
In (God's) fear is the sun, in (God's) fear the moon;
travelling crores of kos, (their journey) has no end.
In (God's) fear are the Siddhas, the Buddhas, the gods and the Naths.
In (God's) fear the skies are stretched out.
In (God's) fear are warriors, the mighty and the brave.
In (God's) fear boatloads (of beings) come and go.
Upon the heads of all, fear is written as their lot.
O Nanak, only the One, the True, the Formless, is without fear. ॥1॥
464.4: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, the Formless One (alone) is without fear; so many other Rams are (but) dust (before him).
So many are the tales of Kaanh, so many the reflections on the Vedas.
So many beggars dance, and wheeling round and round keep the beat.
The players (bajaari) come into the bazaar and set out their show.
They sing (as) kings and queens, and talk wild nonsense.
(They wear) earrings worth a lakh of takas, necklaces worth a lakh of takas;
(but) the bodies they are put on, O Nanak, those bodies turn to ash.
Wisdom is not found by talk; to tell of it is as hard as iron.
It is gained only when it comes by (his) grace; all other cleverness and command come to nothing. ॥2॥
465.1: If you cast your glance of grace, then by (your) grace the True Guru is found.
This soul roamed through many births; then the True Guru made it hear the Shabad.
None is a giver as great as the True Guru; listen, all you people, every one.
Those who rid themselves of self within have found the True One by meeting the True Guru,
(the Guru) who has made (them) understand the True One, Truth itself. ॥4॥
465.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The gharis are all gopis, the pahars (of day and night) Kaanh, Gopal;
wind, water and fire are the ornaments, the moon and the sun the avatars;
the whole earth is (the play's) goods and wealth, and all the world's entanglements are the things it uses.
O Nanak, (the world,) empty of wisdom, is being robbed; Jamkaal has devoured it. ॥1॥
465.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The disciples play (the instruments), and the gurus dance;
they jig their feet and toss their heads;
the dust flies up and settles in their hair.
The onlookers watch, laugh, and make for home.
For the sake of bread they keep the beat,
and fling themselves upon the ground.
They sing as the gopis, they sing as Kaanh,
they sing as Sita and as Ram the king.
The Fearless, the Formless, whose Name is True,
whose making is all the world:
him those servants serve whom (his) grace has uplifted;
for those whose minds are eager (for him), the night (of life) is dew-soaked and sweet.
Those who have learned this teaching through reflection on the Guru's word,
the Gracious One, in his kindness, carries (them) across.
The oil-press, the spinning wheel, the grindstone, the potter's wheel,
the whirlwinds of the desert, many beyond count,
tops, churning-staves, threshing frames,
birds that wheel without pausing for breath,
creatures set on a spike and spun round:
O Nanak, of those that go round there is no count and no end.
Binding (beings) in bonds, he spins them round;
everyone dances by the deeds that have fallen to his lot.
Those who laugh as they dance depart in tears.
(Dancing,) they neither take flight (to a higher state) nor become Siddhas.
Dancing and leaping are (but) the mind's fancy;
O Nanak, those whose minds hold (God's) fear hold (his) love in their minds. ॥2॥
465.4: Your Name is Nirankar (the Formless); taking (your) Name, one does not go to hell.
Soul and body, all is his; give (of what he gives) and then eat; speak of (the giving), and (its merit) is lost.
If you want your own good, do good deeds and (still) be called lowly.
Even if a mighty man would cast it off, old age comes on, putting on its garb.
No one stays (here) when the measure (paai) of life is full. ॥5॥
465.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
With the Muslims it is the praise of the Shariat (the Islamic law); reading it again and again, they reflect:
(God's) servants are those who enter its bond (bandi) to behold (his) vision.
The Hindus praise the Praiseworthy One, through the darshans (their schools of scripture), as beautiful and boundless;
they bathe at the tiraths, make offerings (to images) and worship (them), with the scent of aloe-wood and perfumes.
The yogis, all of them, meditate on the Creator in Sunn, naming him Alakh (the Unseen);
(yet in their meditation) the One of subtle form, whose Name is Niranjan, takes the shape of a body.
In the minds of the charitable, contentment springs up at the thought of giving;
(but) giving and giving, they ask a thousandfold (in return), and the world sings their praise.
Thieves, adulterers and liars, the wicked and the sinful:
some use up what they had and go from here; they too have some task (given them).
In water and on land are beings, in the realms and the worlds, form upon form:
what they say, you alone know; they too are in your care.
O Nanak, the devotees hunger to praise (you); the True Name is (their) support.
Ever in bliss they live, day and night, (as) dust beneath the feet of the virtuous. ॥1॥
466.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The clay of a Muslim('s grave) may come to lie in the potter's lump;
shaping it, (he) makes pots and bricks of it, and as it burns (in the kiln) it cries out.
The poor thing weeps as it burns and burns, and embers keep dropping from it.
O Nanak, the Creator who made the creation, he alone knows (its secret). ॥2॥
466.2: Without the True Guru no one has found (God); without the True Guru no one has found (him).
(God) has placed himself within the True Guru, and has made this plain and proclaimed it.
One who has rid himself of attachment within is free for ever, when the True Guru is met.
Best of all is this understanding: one who has fixed his mind on the True One
has found the Giver, the Life of the world. ॥6॥
466.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
In Haumai (ego) one comes (into the world), in Haumai one goes.
In Haumai one is born, in Haumai one dies.
In Haumai one gives, in Haumai one takes.
In Haumai one earns, in Haumai one loses.
In Haumai one is (now) truthful, (now) false.
In Haumai one weighs sin and merit.
In Haumai one falls (now) into hell, (now) into heaven.
In Haumai one laughs, in Haumai one weeps.
In Haumai one is soiled (with sin), in Haumai one washes (it off).
In Haumai, (proud of) caste and kind, one loses (oneself).
In Haumai one is (now) a fool, in Haumai (now) wise,
(but) does not grasp what liberation and release are.
In Haumai one (chases) Maya, in Haumai (lives under) its shadow.
Acting in Haumai again and again, beings are born (again and again).
When one understands Haumai, then the (Lord's) door comes into sight.
Without this knowledge, one only quarrels, talking and talking.
O Nanak, this record is written by the Hukam:
as (beings) look (upon others), so their own form becomes. ॥1॥
466.4: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
Such is the nature of Haumai: (beings) do the deeds of Haumai.
These are the bonds of Haumai: (beings) fall into the life-forms again and again.
Where does Haumai spring from? By what discipline does it go?
Haumai is by this very Hukam: driven by their past deeds, (beings) wander.
Haumai is a long, lingering disease, but it has a cure as well.
If (God) shows his grace, then (beings) live by the Guru's Shabad.
Nanak says: hear, O people; by this discipline the pains (of Haumai) go. ॥2॥
466.5: Service has been done by the contented, who have meditated on none but the True One.
They have not set foot on (the path of) evil; doing good deeds, they have lived by dharma.
They have broken the world's bonds, and have taken little of grain and water.
(O Lord,) you are the great Giver of gifts; you give each day, and (your giving) ever grows.
By praising (you), they have found (you), the Great One. ॥7॥
467.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Of men, trees, tiraths, riverbanks, clouds and fields,
of islands, worlds, spheres, continents and universes,
of the sources of life, egg-born, womb-born, earth-born and sweat-born,
of lakes, mountains and creatures, he knows the measure, O Nanak.
O Nanak, having brought forth the beings, (God) takes care of them all.
The Creator who made the creation must also see to its care.
That Creator who brought forth the world takes thought for it.
To him I bow, hail to him; his court stands for ever unbroken.
O Nanak, without the True Name, what is the frontal mark, what the sacred thread? ॥1॥
467.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Lakhs of good deeds and kindnesses, lakhs of acts of merit approved (by the world),
lakhs of austerities at tiraths, yoga in the stillness of Sahaj in the wilds,
lakhs of feats of valour, the breath of life let go on the field of battle,
lakhs of ways of fixing the attention, lakhs of (discourses on) knowledge and of meditations, and the Puranas read and recited:
(before) the Creator who made the creation and wrote down (all) coming and going,
O Nanak, (all these) clevernesses are worthless; his grace is the true mark (of acceptance). ॥2॥
467.3: (O Lord,) you alone are the True Master, who have made Truth, nothing but Truth, prevail.
Whoever you give it to receives Truth; then such ones live the Truth.
Those in whose hearts (the Guru) has set Truth to dwell have found Truth through meeting the True Guru.
Fools do not know the Truth; the manmukhs have wasted their lives.
Why did (such a one) come into the world? ॥8॥
467.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One may read and read till carts are loaded, read and read till caravans are filled (with books);
read and read till a boat is laden, read and read till pits are packed full;
one may read for as many years as there are, year upon year, read for as many months as there are;
one may read for as long as life lasts, read for as many breaths as there are:
(Even so,) O Nanak, in (God's) reckoning one thing alone counts; all else is the idle babble of Haumai. ॥1॥
467.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
However much one writes and reads, so much does one fret and burn (within).
However many tiraths one tours, so much the more one prattles.
(One) has put on many guises and given the body pain:
endure, O soul, what you have done yourself.
(One who) has eaten no grain has lost the taste (of life);
he has suffered much pain, for something other (than the Name) has pleased him.
(One) wears no clothes, and is in torment day and night.
(One) has gone astray in silence: asleep, how can he wake without the Guru?
(One) goes barefoot, and reaps what he has done.
(One) has eaten what is foul and put ash on his head:
the blind fool has lost his honour.
Without the Name, nothing is accepted.
(One) lives in the wilds, at tombs and cremation grounds:
the blind man does not know (the way), and afterwards repents.
One who meets the True Guru finds peace,
and enshrines the Lord's Name in the mind.
O Nanak, one on whom (God) casts his glance of grace finds (the Guru);
free from hope and anxiety, he burns away Haumai through the Shabad. ॥2॥
468.1: (O Lord,) your devotees are dear to your mind; singing (your) praises, they look beautiful at (your) door.
O Nanak, those without (his) grace find no shelter at the door; they wander about.
Some do not understand their own origin, and, having nothing, make much of themselves.
I am a humble minstrel (dhadhi) of low caste; others call themselves high-born.
(The company of) those who meditate on you is what I ask for. ॥9॥
468.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The king is falsehood, the subjects are falsehood, all the world is falsehood.
Pavilions are falsehood, palaces are falsehood, and he who sits in them is falsehood.
Gold is falsehood, silver is falsehood, and he who wears them is falsehood.
The body is falsehood, clothes are falsehood, and beauty beyond measure is falsehood.
Husband is falsehood, wife is falsehood; worn out (in it), they come to ruin.
The false one's love is fixed in falsehood, and he has forgotten the Creator.
With whom should one make friends? The whole world is passing away.
Falsehood is sweet, falsehood is honey; falsehood drowns the whole boatload (of beings).
Nanak humbly prays: without you, (all) is falsehood, nothing but falsehood. ॥1॥
468.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Truth is known only when the True One is in the heart;
(then) the filth of falsehood comes off, and (one) washes the body clean.
Truth is known only when (one) bears love for the True One;
hearing the Name, the mind blossoms with joy, and then one finds the door of liberation.
Truth is known only when the soul knows the (true) way of life:
making ready the earth of the body, it puts into it the Creator's seed (the Name).
Truth is known only when (one) takes true teaching (from the Guru),
knows how to show compassion to living beings, and gives something in charity and good works.
Truth is known only when (one) dwells at the tirath of the soul within,
and, having asked the True Guru, stays seated (there) and makes his home (there).
Truth is the cure for all (ills); it washes sins away and drives them out.
Nanak humbly prays before those who have Truth in their lap. ॥2॥
468.4: For me the gift (to ask for) is the dust from beneath (the Sants') feet; if it is obtained, let it be put to the forehead.
Let false greed be given up, and, single-minded, let the Unseen One be meditated on.
Such fruit is reaped as is the work one does.
If it is so written from the start, then the dust of such ones is obtained.
(Leaning on one's) small understanding, service is lost. ॥10॥
468.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
A famine of Truth has come, falsehood holds sway; in the blackness of Kalyug, (people have become) ghouls.
Those who sowed the seed (of the Name) have gone with honour; how now can split grain sprout?
Seed sprouts if it is whole, and the season too is the best of seasons.
O Nanak, without the mordant, raw cloth does not take the (fast) colour.
In the fear (of God) let (the mind) be set on the khumb, and let effort be the mordant for the cloth (of the body).
O Nanak, if (the mind) is dyed in devotion, not a trace of falsehood (remains). ॥1॥
468.6: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Greed and sin are the two, king and minister (mahta), and falsehood has become the chief (sikdar).
Lust is the deputy (naib), summoned and consulted; he sits with them, deliberating again and again.
The subjects, blind and without knowledge, stuff the fire (of the rulers' craving) with carrion (bribes).
Those (called) wise dance, play instruments, put on guises and adorn themselves.
They shout aloud, sing of battles, and expound the tales of warriors.
Foolish pandits love to amass (wealth) by cunning and argument.
The pious do pious deeds and waste them, asking (in return) for the door of liberation.
(Some) call themselves celibates but do not know the way; they leave hearth and home and sit (apart).
Everyone is perfect in his own eyes; no one calls himself lacking.
O Nanak, only when the weight of honour (from God) is put in the other pan does (one) prove truly weighed. ॥2॥
469.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
What is ordained, O Nanak, shall sound forth (come to light); the True One himself watches over (all).
All have made their leaps (and tried their strength), but what the Creator does, that comes to pass.
Hereafter there is no caste and no force; hereafter the beings (one meets) are new (strangers).
Those few whose honour counts in the reckoning, they alone are good. ॥3॥
469.2: Those on whom you cast your grace from the very first have then meditated on the Master.
It is not in these creatures' power to do anything; you have brought forth a world of many kinds.
Some you unite (with yourself); others you have led astray from yourself.
By the Guru's grace you are known (by the one) to whom you have made yourself understood,
and (that one) has merged, in Sahaj, in the True One. ॥11॥
469.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Sorrow has become the remedy and comfort the disease, for when there is comfort, then (your remembrance) is not there.
You are the Creator, the Doer (of all); I am nothing; when I would do (anything) myself, it does not come about. ॥1॥
469.4: I am a sacrifice to you, who dwell within your creation;
469.5: Your light is in the creation, and in every light you are known; undivided and whole, you fill all things.
You are the True Master, and lovely is your praise; whoever has offered it has crossed over.
Says Nanak, (all these are) the Creator's doings: whatever is to be done, he is doing. ॥2॥
469.6: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
The way of the yogi is knowledge; the way of the Brahmins is the Veda;
the way of the Khatri is valour; the way of the Shudra is the service of others;
the way of all is (the remembrance of) the One; if anyone knows this secret,
Nanak is his servant; he himself is (the image of) Niranjan, the Lord. ॥3॥
469.7: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
The one Krishna (the Lord) is the soul of all the gods, and the soul too of the gods of the gods;
(in all) is the soul of Vasudev (the Lord); if anyone knows this secret,
Nanak is his servant; he himself is (the image of) Niranjan, the Lord. ॥4॥
469.8: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Water stays held only within a pitcher, (yet) without water no pitcher is made;
(so) the mind stays steady only when held by wisdom, (yet) without the Guru there is no wisdom. ॥5॥
469.9: If the learned one is a sinner, the unlettered one who is good is not punished.
As are the deeds one labours at, so is the name one comes to be known by.
Let no such game be played as would make one lose on reaching the Lord's court.
Of the learned and the unlettered alike, the case is weighed hereafter;
whoever goes headstrong, by his own will, is punished hereafter. ॥12॥
470.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, the body that is the meru (the crown of all bodies, the human one) has one chariot and one charioteer;
age after age they are changed again; the wise understand this.
In Satjug the chariot is of contentment, and dharma the charioteer in front;
in Treta the chariot is of continence, and might the charioteer in front;
in Duapar the chariot is of austerity, and sat (upright conduct) the charioteer in front;
in Kalyug the chariot is of fire, and falsehood the charioteer in front. ॥1॥
470.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The Sama (Veda) calls the Master Setambar (the white-robed), who dwells in truth; (in its age, people) abide in truth;
among the gods, the Name of Ram is the sun;
by taking the Name, sins depart;
In the Yajur (Veda), Chandravali was beguiled by force, and (the Master's name) became Kaanh Krishna, the Yadav;
he brought the Parjat (tree) for the gopi, and made merry in Brindaban.
In Kalyug the Atharva Veda came (to the fore), and (the Master's) name became Khuda and Allah;
taking blue cloth, they wore garments (of it), and the Turks and Pathans held sway.
All four Vedas came to be (held) true;
those who read and ponder them find four (different) teachings (in them).
One who, worshipping with loving devotion, calls himself lowly,
470.3: I am a sacrifice to the True Guru, meeting whom (I have) kept the Master in mind;
who, giving his teaching, has given (me) the collyrium of wisdom, by which with these eyes (I) have seen the world (as it is).
Those traders who left the Master and clung to another have drowned.
The True Guru is the ship; rare is the one who has understood (this);
(him the Guru) in his grace has carried across. ॥13॥
470.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The simmal tree is straight, very tall and very stout;
(the birds) that come to it in hope: why do they go away disappointed?
(Because) its fruits are insipid, its flowers tasteless, and its leaves of no use.
O Nanak, sweetness and lowliness are the very core of virtues and good deeds.
Everyone bows for his own sake; no one bows for another's.
Put on the scales and weighed, the (pan) that sinks is the heavier.
The sinner who slays deer bows double;
(but) what comes of bowing the head, when (people) go on with impure hearts? ॥1॥
470.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(The pandit) reads the books, says the sandhya prayers, and disputes;
he worships stone (idols), and sits in trance like a heron;
lies are on his lips, (decked out) like fine ornaments;
three times a day he ponders the three-footed (Gayatri);
a rosary round his neck, a tilak on his brow;
two dhotis, and a cloth over his head.
If he knew the work of (worshipping) God,
(he would see that) all these rites are surely hollow.
Says Nanak, one should meditate (on God) with firm faith,
(but) without the True Guru one does not find the way. ॥2॥
470.6: Leaving the lovely garment (of the body) and its beauty in the world, one has to go;
the bad and the good one has done, one must oneself reap.
(One who) gave orders as his mind pleased must go hereafter by a narrow road;
stripped bare, he is driven to hell, and then he looks dreadful indeed.
Having done wrong, he must repent. ॥14॥
471.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Compassion the cotton, contentment the thread, continence the knots and upright conduct the twist:
such is the soul's sacred thread; O pandit, if you have it, put it on (me).
It does not break, no dirt clings to it, it is not burned, nor is it lost.
Blessed, O Nanak, are the people who go (on their way) wearing it round their necks.
(This thread) you had brought for four cowries and, seated in the chauka, put it on (your patron);
you whispered instruction in (his) ear, and the Brahmin became (his) guru.
He died, it fell away, and he went without a thread. ॥1॥
471.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(One commits) countless thefts, countless adulteries, countless lies and countless abuses;
countless frauds and breaches of trust, kept secret within, night and day.
From cotton the thread is spun; the Brahmin comes and twists it;
a goat is killed, cooked and eaten, and everyone says: (the thread) is on.
When it grows old it is cast aside, and then another is put on.
O Nanak, were there strength in the thread, the thread would not break. ॥2॥
471.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
By believing in the Name, honour springs up; praise (of God) is the true thread;
(with it, honour) is gained in the Lord's court; this pure thread will not break. ॥3॥
471.4: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
There is no thread on the senses, no thread (to hold him back) from women;
(so) morning after morning his beard is spat upon.
No thread on the feet, no thread on the hands;
no thread on the tongue, no thread on the eyes.
Without a thread himself he wanders about,
yet twisting threads, he puts them on others.
He takes a fee and performs marriages,
and, taking out his almanac, shows (people) the way.
Hear and see, O people, this wonder:
blind in mind, and his name is Wise. ॥4॥
471.5: When the Master grows merciful and shows grace, he will have (one) do that very work (which pleases him).
That servant alone serves whom (the Master) makes obey his Hukam.
By obeying the Hukam (he) is approved, and then he will reach the Master's mansion.
Doing what pleases the Master, he will gain the fruit his mind longed for;
then he will go to the Lord's court robed in honour. ॥15॥
471.6: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
You levy a tax on the cow and the Brahmin; by the cow-dung (you plaster with) no one crosses over.
Dhoti, tilak and rosary (you wear), (yet) you eat the grain of the mlechhas.
Indoors you worship, (outside) you read the Kateb; your way of life, brother, is the Turks'.
taking the Naam, you will cross over. ॥1॥
471.7: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Those who devour men say the namaz;
those who ply the knife have the sacred thread at their necks.
In their homes the Brahmins blow the conch;
they too relish the same flavours.
False is the capital, false the trade;
by speaking lies they get their food.
Modesty and dharma dwell far away (from them);
O Nanak, falsehood fills every place.
A tilak on the forehead, an ochre dhoti round the waist,
(and) a knife in the hand: (they are) butchers of the world.
Wearing blue clothes, they find favour (with the rulers);
taking their bread from the mlechhas, they worship the Puranas.
Their food is a goat slaughtered with the words of a foreign tongue,
(yet they say:) no one is to step onto our chauka.
The chauka is laid out and a line drawn (around it);
and the false ones come and sit upon it.
(They say:) take care, lest it be defiled, lest it be defiled;
this food of ours will be spoiled.
With defiled bodies they do wicked deeds,
and with soiled minds they rinse their mouths.
Says Nanak, let the True One be meditated on;
if there is purity, then the True One is found. ॥2॥
472.1: (God) holds everyone in his mind, and, watching (them), moves them along under his eye.
He himself bestows greatness, and he himself has (beings) do their deeds.
Greater than the great is he, and vast his earth; one by one he sets each to his task.
If he turns his look against them, he makes sultans (worth no more than) grass;
they beg at the door, and no one puts alms (in their bowl). ॥16॥
472.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If a thief robs a house, and, having robbed it, gives (the goods) for his forebears,
then in the world beyond the goods are recognised, and (so) he makes thieves of his forebears.
The hands of the go-between (the Brahmin) are cut off: such is the justice (God) does.
O Nanak, in the world beyond one receives only what one earns, toils for and gives (with one's own hands). ॥1॥
472.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
As a woman's monthly course comes to her time after time,
(so) in the mouth of the false dwells the defilement (of falsehood), and day after day he comes to grief.
They are not called pure who (merely) wash the body and sit down (as pure);
O Nanak, they alone are pure in whose mind he (God) has come to dwell. ॥2॥
472.4: (Those who have) saddled horses swift as the wind, and harems decked out in every colour,
(who) have set up houses, pavilions and mansions and sit (in them), having spread out a display,
(who) take the pleasures their minds desire, but do not know the Lord: they lose (the game of life).
Giving orders, they ate (their fill), and gazing at their palaces forgot death;
old age came upon them, undone by their youth. ॥17॥
472.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If Sutak is to be believed in, then Sutak is everywhere:
in cow-dung and in wood, too, the worm comes to life;
of all the grains of corn there are, not one is without life;
first of all, water itself is a living thing, by which every being is kept green (alive).
How then can Sutak be kept away? Sutak falls in the very kitchen.
O Nanak, Sutak is not removed in this way; (divine) knowledge washes it off. ॥1॥
472.6: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
